blocks.x: Cyber & Zero-Trust applied to Property & Casualty. This page sets out the operating context, the delivery pattern we run, the services and platforms involved, and the outcomes we commit to.

P&C economics live in two moments: pricing the risk before the event and handling the claim after it. Both are decision factories — rate against exposure and catastrophe models, settle against policy language and fraud signals — and both reward carriers whose document and data machinery is industrialized.

items: Third-party handlers hold sensitive claims data with uneven controls; the carrier owns the headline risk.
FNOL, estimates, medical and police files arrive as documents; triage takes days and leakage hides in the queue.

blocks.x: The pattern composes Compliance, Audit & Digital Trust, AI Security & Model Protection, Threat Intelligence & Managed SOC from the Cybersecurity & Zero-Trust tower, wired into the unit's workflows (FNOL and claims triage, Estimate review and leakage control, Commercial risk surveying) on Dataq Sentinel and Dataq Compass. Governance inherits the sector frame — Rate filing regimes among others — with evidence generated by the delivery itself.

items: Secure at the control plane: posture, workload and data security engineered into the platform.
Secure the models themselves: prompt-injection defense, agent containment and AI red-teaming.
Assume breach, plan recovery: resilience engineered, rehearsed and measured.
Third-party tiers, access reviews and evidence automation (handler risk governed)

blocks.x: At industry level, the same pattern

At Insurance & Risk level this capability reads as: third-party risk tiers, access reviews and evidence automation (vendor assessments automated). The sub-industry page narrows it to the unit's workflows, regimes and KPIs.

The engagement cadence below is the standard pattern for this capability. Weeks 1–2 lock the baseline: the current metric is measured with your team and signed before build starts. Weeks 3–8 deliver the pilot on bounded scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with a control owner named on your side. Weeks 9–12 industrialize what worked: runbooks, monitoring, enablement and a measured delta against the signed baseline. Anything that misses its gate is stopped or redirected with a documented decision, not quietly extended.
